Each is inside “coloração azulada ou arroxeada da pele e/ou das mucosas”, printed identically under the three headings (B024-02).
The wording fits the description, but the utterance frames the colour as an unexplained purplish change without trauma and an un-keyed entry could not be ruled out (B024-01).
“A pele das minhas mãos parecia arroxeada … sem ter batido nelas”: the adjective of the Equimoses description plus a denial of trauma; distribution of the colour not stated (B024-01).
Purplish fingertips, no mark or spots, and the added detail excludes a stain that washes off, not trauma (B024-04).
The colour is attributed to the skin under (121) or beside (128) the nails; the entry is an excluded anatomical heading in the inventory (B024-03).

findings.issue: Index 126: “Meu filho perguntou por que a pele das minhas mãos parecia arroxeada. Olhei e percebi a mesma mudança, sem ter batido nelas.” The wording supports Cianose by the letter of the description. The only added detail is a denial of trauma, which frames the finding as an unexplained bruise. APARELHO HEMOLINFOPOIÉTICO > Equimoses is described as “Manchas arroxeadas maiores e planas na pele, decorrentes da infiltração de sangue no tecido subcutâneo.” and uses the same adjective. The utterance does not say whether the colour is diffuse or in patches, symmetrical, or related to cold. The story rationale states “não são lesões hemorrágicas delimitadas”, a fact that is not in the utterance.

findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the single key. Every utterance locates a pressure, pain, tightness or discomfort in the chest; none mentions breathing, heartbeat, burning, fear or threat, breast, skin, touch or movement, and several deny one of these explicitly (131 skin, 134 throat, 136 touch, 137 breast, 138 skin). For 133 and 135 the reviewer reads the source wording “pressão … ou desconforto no peito” as covering weight and tightness when breathing is not mentioned; teaching confirmation recommended.

findings.issue: No rationale names a symptom or term of another group. Cianose stories: each has its own first rationale; the cardiovascular and vascular-peripheral evidence entries reuse one stock sentence that restates the source description (“O relato explicita a manifestação definida em Cianose: coloração azulada ou arroxeada da pele e/ou  das mucosas A posição no roteiro não define etiologia.”), with a missing full stop after “mucosas” in the cardiovascular copy. Index 120 and others say “as três entradas equivalentes”. Index 126: the rationale asserts “não são lesões hemorrágicas delimitadas”, which the utterance does not state. Index 124: “sem atribuição vascular ou respiratória causal” is a disclaimer, not a reason. Dor stories: each has its own rationale. Index 139: “não há relação postural específica que permita outro termo” refers to the sentence itself, but the script has no posture-related pain term (its posture-related entries are breathlessness terms). Index 130: “definição ampla de Dor cardiovascular” is acceptable shorthand for the entry under that heading. No gender is stated in a rationale that is absent from its sentence.
findings.resolution: Passing stories are not held for this. Since the app shows the rationale to the student, the stock sentence could be replaced by the story-specific one on all three paths, the missing full stop fixed, and the tail of the rationale of index 139 dropped. For the held story the rationale gap is part of B024-01.

findings.issue: Most second sentences are denials written to close alternatives. Some read as authored rather than spoken: index 127 “nem sombra da iluminação”; index 134 “O que quero relatar é essa dor, não nos braços ou na garganta”; index 137 “Não estou falando de uma dor na mama”; index 138 “não era no cinto nem na pele”. Index 122: “de um jeito diferente” is vague. Indices 131, 134, 136 and 139 use the word “dor”, which is the label of the keyed entry (137 uses it negated); the task for the student is then mostly the heading, which is unavoidable for an entry whose label is a lay word.
findings.resolution: None of these opens another term. Suggested polish for a later edit: 134 and 138 could state the location positively (“bem no meio do peito, por dentro”) instead of listing where the pain is not.

findings.issue: The inventory and the stories' sourceQuote record the Cianose description with two spaces (“e/ou  das mucosas”); the PDF text extraction returns single spaces. The vascular-peripheral copy ends with a full stop, the other two do not. The respiratory Cianose line is on p.3, under a heading printed on p.2. The Equimoses entry is extracted out of reading order (“Equimoses: subcutâneo.” followed by “Manchas arroxeadas maiores e planas na pele, decorrentes da infiltração de sangue no tecido”); Petéquias, Ansiedade, the mio-ósteo-articular Dor entry and Pirose break across lines.
findings.resolution: Quotes were compared with whitespace and the fi ligature normalised; sourceExactLine carries the extraction, sourceQuote the story's own string. For entries that break across lines (Petéquias, Pirose, Ansiedade, mio-ósteo-articular Dor) the evidence quote is the term label followed by the inventory description, whitespace-normalised. Not visually verified in this run.

findings.issue: The thirty evidence entries of the Cianose stories cite the batch reference nhs-cyanosis-next02 (NHS — Blue or grey skin or lips (cyanosis)). The ten Dor evidence entries cite no reference. The reference was not re-opened by this reviewer.
